title: Karta Workloads

options.content:
# Karta Workloads
Live workload identity, status, CPU and memory from the current exporter. Open a workload to inspect its Components and Pods. GPU readings on this cluster are simulated. GPU utilization alone does not establish application idleness.

This layout was restored from the saved playground. `karta_demo:*` rules adapt the old labels; exporter metrics remain unchanged.

panels.title: Workloads
panels.description: Distinct observed workload UIDs, including workloads with zero currently attributed Pods. Namespace and workload filters apply; component filters do not. Deleted workloads disappear from current inventory after exporter reconciliation and Prometheus staleness.

panels.title: Pods
panels.description: Unique current Pod attributions after exporter replica deduplication and conflict rejection. Workload-level scope; component filters do not apply.

panels.title: Workload health
panels.description: Healthy described workload lifetimes divided by all described workload lifetimes for the selected namespace/workload. Includes workloads with zero Pods. Unknown if an exporter target is down. This is observation health, not workload readiness. Workload-level scope; component filters do not apply.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Total measured container CPU for selected attributed Pods. CPU fixtures may intentionally sleep; low activity is expected. Displayed in millicores: 1000 mCPU = one CPU core. Workload-level scope; component filters do not apply.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Total observed container working set for selected attributed Pods. Workload-level scope; component filters do not apply.

panels.title: Scrape health
panels.description: Fraction of discovered exporter targets whose latest scrape succeeded. Independent of namespace/workload filters; does not assert expected target discovery completeness.

panels.title: Top 8 workloads by CPU
panels.description: Measured container resources summed across all attributed components of each workload UID. Component filters do not apply. Top eight can change over time; absence is not zero. Click to inspect the exact workload UID.

panels.title: Top 8 workloads by memory
panels.description: Measured container resources summed across all attributed components of each workload UID. Component filters do not apply. Top eight can change over time; absence is not zero. Click to inspect the exact workload UID.

panels.title: Workload CPU over time
panels.description: Measured container resources summed across all attributed components of each workload UID. Component filters do not apply. Top eight can change over time; absence is not zero. Click to inspect the exact workload UID.

panels.title: Workload memory over time
panels.description: Measured container resources summed across all attributed components of each workload UID. Component filters do not apply. Top eight can change over time; absence is not zero. Click to inspect the exact workload UID.

panels.title: Reported workload phases
panels.description: Independent phase-match counts across described workloads. The KEP permits several phases to match one workload, so these counts overlap and must not be summed into an inventory total. Component filtering does not change this workload-wide view.

panels.title: Unhealthy described workloads
panels.description: Zero means every currently described workload in the selected workload scope is healthy. No data means no workloads or an exporter scrape is down. Uninstalled API definitions are excluded.

panels.title: Observed workloads / click a workload for components and Pods
panels.description: One row per namespace and workload UID, including completed and zero-Pod workloads still observed by Karta. Observation health is separate from lifecycle phases. Exact UID is used for drilldown. No missing resource samples are converted to zero.

panels.title: Workload lifecycle / each matching phase shown
panels.description: Each matching phase is a separate row for the exact workload UID. Karta phases may overlap; Completed and Initializing can both match one workload. This is not a mutually exclusive state machine.

panels.title: Top 8 CPU components
panels.description: Current top eight component/instance CPU totals; replica groups are summed. Click a bar to focus that workload/component. Source container series are deduplicated before attribution. Displayed in millicores: 1000 mCPU = one CPU core.

panels.title: Top 8 memory components
panels.description: Current top eight component/instance working sets; replica groups are summed. Click a bar to focus that workload/component.

panels.title: CPU over time
panels.description: Top eight components at each sample. Series can enter and leave the top eight. Select a workload/component for stable focused comparisons. Displayed in millicores: 1000 mCPU = one CPU core.

panels.title: Memory over time
panels.description: Top eight components at each sample. Gaps represent absent samples, not zero usage.

panels.title: Pod distribution by component
panels.description: Top ten component groups by number of attributed Pods.

panels.title: EXPORTER DIAGNOSTICS  /  independent of workload filters
Scrape duration by replica
panels.description: Time Prometheus spent scraping each exporter replica. A faster small demo scrape is not a 100k-workload scalability result.

panels.title: Attribution sample age
panels.description: Age of latest exporter attribution sample. Normal sawtooth follows the 30-second scrape interval. Missing series cannot establish freshness.

panels.title: Scrape payload samples
panels.description: Number of samples returned by each exporter scrape, before relabeling. Useful for spotting cardinality changes; independent of workload filters.

panels.title: DETAILS  /  identities, phases, and optional API definitions
Pod attribution details
panels.description: Exact deduplicated Pod-to-workload identities for the selected workload/component. Unknown metadata remains visible.

panels.title: Resource watches and discovery failures
panels.description: Actual exporter failures, independent of the selected workload. Empty means no currently reported failures; exporter scrape health must also be checked.

panels.title: GPU requests in Running demo Pods
panels.description: Kubernetes GPU requests for Running Pods, joined to valid Karta attribution. Devices in this cluster are simulated. This is requested capacity, not measured physical allocation.

targets.expr: sum(max by(namespace,pod,container) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace",resource="nvidia_com_gpu"}) * on(namespace,pod) group_left(workload,workload_uid) karta:pod_attribution:unique{namespace=~"$namespace",workload=~"$workload"} * on(namespace,pod) group_left() (max by(namespace,pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"$namespace",phase="Running"}) == 1))

panels.title: Simulated GPU utilization by workload (maximum device)
panels.description: Fake GPU telemetry, not physical GPU work or proof of application activity. exported_namespace and exported_pod are normalized before the Pod-name join. Name reuse remains a limitation.

description: Live Karta workload attribution and status. CPU and memory measure real demo containers. GPU capacity and utilization are simulated by the existing fake GPU installation.
